article_title: Learning: One definition to rule them all?
citation: Martin Lövdén, Isabelle Hansson & Toms Voits. (2026). Learning: One definition to rule them all? npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-026-00441-7
title: Umbrella definition of learning as environment-informed information processing that changes system properties and behavioral potential
description: The article proposes a unifying definition: "a system's processing of information from its environment, resulting in a change of system properties that alter its behavioral potential and reactions to this information." It combines structural and functional perspectives: the structural aspect is acknowledged but not specified, while the functional component guides operational definitions. It is intended to apply across disciplines, organisms, machines, and groups, with discipline-specific operationalizations of information and behavior.
requirements: Requires discipline-specific definitions of the terms information and behavior to reach acceptable precision
constraints: Excludes maturation and senescence to the extent these are not based on processing of information from the environment
target_learners: Organisms, artificial systems, groups, and cellular networks, as systems that learn
target_learning_goals: Theorizing and cross-disciplinary communication about what learning is
examples: The article evaluates the definition against desiderata for a good cross-disciplinary concept and contrasts it with prior definitions such as Barron's structured-updating formulation
